oneOf.description:
The first message: the client's API version (`"1.0"`), name and
features.
Start a call (its id is the frame's).
The daemon's version, host and the caller's identity and role.

Lifecycle events from `since` (a cursor from an earlier read), at
most `limit`, of these `kinds` (all when empty).

The tracked flows of a node, or of every node, that `query` selects
(#303; API 1.1).

Follow an operation started earlier (by this or another client):
its events so far, then the rest.
A stream of notifications: of one lab, or of all with `lab: null`.
The deploy plan, without deploying.
What an apply would change, without changing it.
Drift between the lab and its topology.
Orphans and stale labs on the host.

Delete the tracked flows `query` selects, on a node or every node
(#303; API 1.1).
A network's per-pair impairment from `src` to `dst`; `None` clears it.

Run a command; its output streams as data, then `Exited`. With
`stdin`, the client streams input; with `tty`, it runs on a pty.
An interactive shell on a pty of `rows` × `cols`.
Capture packets on an endpoint; the pcap streams as data.
The lab as an `.nlz` archive, streamed as data.
Leave a long operation running and stop following it.
End of the call's stdin.

keep_conntrack.description:
Keep the tracked flows of the NAT rules the apply changes; they are
deleted otherwise, so they take the new rules (#303).

CaptureFilter.description:
What a capture keeps (`capture`): every condition set must hold, the
port lists match any of theirs, and `not` keeps the rest instead. The
CLI's `--filter-*` flags say the same.

expression.description:
A tcpdump expression instead of the conditions above: only a
daemon built with `legacy-tcpdump-filter` (and `tcpdump`) compiles
one.

ConntrackQuery.description:
What a conntrack listing or flush selects (#303): every field it sets
must hold. Addresses and ports are the flow's original direction, as it
began (before NAT).

dport.description: The destination port (with `proto` tcp or udp).

dst.description: The destination, an address or a CIDR.

sport.description: The source port (with `proto` tcp or udp).

src.description: The source, an address or a CIDR.

status.description:
Status bits the flow has, nft's names: `snat`, `dnat`, `assured`,
`seen-reply`, `confirmed`, `expected`, `dying`.

force.description: Destroy a lab of that name first.

strict.description: A failed assertion fails the deploy.

suffix.description: Appended to the lab's name and prefix.

Direction.description:
Which way an impairment acts on an endpoint's link: out of it (its
egress), into it (the peer's egress), or both.

ImpairmentSpec.description:
An impairment (netem), every knob optional: what `impair` sets and the
GUI's editor edits. Values are in NLL's units (`"10ms"`, `"1%"`,
`"100mbit"`).

SourceBundle.description:
Where a lab's topology came from, sent with a deploy: the file's text
and the files it imports (keyed by their path relative to it), so the
daemon never reads a client's files by path.

path.description: The entry file's path, as the client knows it (for messages only).

oneOf.description: Labs appearing, changing, going away.
The lab's lifecycle events (deployed, applied, impaired, …).
Interfaces going up or down, processes exiting.
Metrics snapshots, every interval.
A new topology after an apply or restore.
Progress of operations.
Changes nobody made through nlink-lab (hand edits).

WaitSpec.description:
A condition a `wait_for` (or a spawn) waits for. Conditions given
together must all hold.

listening.description: A port a process of the node listens on.

log.description: A regex a (spawned) process's log line matches.
